questions.question: What are the three span categories in the OTel GenAI semantic conventions?
options: Request, Response, Error
Model/client spans, Agent spans, Tool spans
Input, Processing, Output
Application, Framework, Infrastructure
questions.explanation: The GenAI SIG defines three span categories: Model/client spans (raw LLM calls), Agent spans (create_agent and invoke_agent), and Tool spans (one per tool invocation, connected to the agent span by parent-child relation).

questions.question: When should an invoke_agent span use CLIENT vs INTERNAL kind?
options: CLIENT for Python agents, INTERNAL for JavaScript agents
CLIENT for remote agent services (OpenAI Assistants, Bedrock Agents), INTERNAL for in-process agent frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, local ReAct)
CLIENT for production, INTERNAL for development
CLIENT when the agent calls external APIs, INTERNAL when it does not
questions.explanation: CLIENT kind is for calls to remote agent services (OpenAI Assistants API, AWS Bedrock Agents). INTERNAL kind is for in-process agent frameworks running locally (LangChain, CrewAI, local ReAct loops).

questions.question: What is the default content capture behavior in the GenAI conventions?
options: Always capture all inputs and outputs
Instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture inputs/outputs by default; capture is opt-in
Capture only errors and exceptions
Capture only system instructions, not user messages
questions.explanation: The GenAI conventions specify that instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture inputs/outputs by default. Capture is opt-in via gen_ai.system_instructions, gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages. In production, store content externally and reference by ID.

questions.question: What is gen_ai.data_source.id used for?
options: Identifying which database the agent is connected to
For RAG: identifying which corpus or store was consulted during retrieval
Identifying the training data source for the model
Tracking which tool registry is being used
questions.explanation: gen_ai.data_source.id is a GenAI attribute for RAG use cases that identifies which corpus or retrieval store was consulted. This enables tracing which knowledge source contributed to a specific agent response.

questions.question: How do you opt in to the stable preview of GenAI semantic conventions as of March 2026?
options: Set OTEL_GENAI_ENABLED=true
Set OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental
Set GENAI_CONVENTIONS_VERSION=latest
Install the genai-stable package
questions.explanation: Most GenAI conventions are experimental as of March 2026. To opt into the stable preview, set: OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental

questions.question: What are the four key gen_ai provider names expected in the spec?
options: gpt, claude, gemini, llama
anthropic, openai, aws.bedrock, google.vertex
anthropic, openai, google, microsoft
claude, gpt-4, gemini, titan
questions.explanation: The GenAI spec defines gen_ai.provider.name as: anthropic, openai, aws.bedrock, google.vertex. Consistent provider names across teams allow cross-provider dashboards to work without manual mapping.
